events.title: Gilleonan bores the first bone pipes
events.body: At Cnoc àrsaidh, Gilleonan bores four holes along a hollow bird-bone and finds a note he can raise and lower at will; children of three households gather to hear him play, the first instrument the island's tellers count as more than a horn blown flat.

events.title: Three cats turn back at the pass
events.body: Watchers along Imrich nam Pantar see three great cats, on three different days, halt at the throat of the highest pass and turn back south rather than finish the crossing every household's memory says they always finish.

events.title: The households along the road store double
events.body: Reading the cats' turning for a kinder ground left behind and a harder winter ahead, the households nearest the pass lay in double against a season no cat that year would risk crossing into, and go short of nothing before the thaw.

events.title: Iain drives cattle onto Imrich nam Pantar
events.body: With the household's grazing run thin, Iain of Muileann bhàn takes four men and forty head of thin cattle up into the passes against the custom that keeps the crossing season's road clear of herds, meaning to bring them down fattened within the week.

events.title: The foster-son of Dùn ìseal comes home
events.body: He walks Rathad an t-Salainn east with a train of laden pack-beasts and three of An Cnoc Ruadh's household, and comes in sight of the hill of Rìghrean na Cloiche on the seventh evening, four-and-twenty years after he first walked the same road west at six years old.

events.title: Calum Ciar does not know his own brother
events.body: Meeting An Cnoc Ruadh's train at the gate in his mother's stead, Calum Ciar asks the fosterling which of the household he might be, a lake wind and four-and-twenty years having left nothing in him his brother's eye could fasten on as kin.

events.title: Eilidh Ghlas knows her son at the door
events.body: Carried out to the hall door, Eilidh speaks her younger son's name before he has said a word to tell her who he is, and weeps and holds him a long while before she lets even her elder son greet him in turn.

events.title: The salt refrain is sung at the pans of Baile ghorm
events.body: At the fires of the salt-rakers he teaches, without meaning to teach anything, the four-line refrain sung at the crust on An Cnoc Ruadh's own lake shore. An old raker keeps it whole from a single hearing, and it runs on afterward at the sea-shore pans in words An Cnoc Ruadh itself can no longer wholly construe.

events.title: Rìghrean na Cloiche' list keeps him no name
events.body: When the reciters after Eilidh set down her reign and her sons, Calum Ciar takes his place among the holders as every holder before him; of the one who went to An Cnoc Ruadh and came home grown, no year, no reign and no deed is written, and the list stands as if she bore only the one son.

events.title: The panthers take thirty head in the night
events.body: On the fourth night a string of cats, the last and largest of that year's crossing, comes down on the herd; by first light thirty of the forty head are taken or scattered beyond finding.

events.title: Iain is lamed in the dark
events.body: Throwing himself clear of a claw he never clearly sees, Iain twists his leg under him against a hidden stone; it sets crooked at the hip, and he walks from that winter with a stick and a roll to one side.

events.title: Baile dhomhain cuts the first season's sign
events.body: The households of Baile dhomhain begin cutting a mark into every gatepost at the start of the crossing season and scraping it away at its close, the first mark the island's tellers know cut for a season rather than for any single event.

events.title: Caol bheag names its boats for the winds
events.body: The fishing households of Caol bheag fix the custom of naming each boat for the wind it is built to fish in, holding a boat unlucky under any other wind and never giving a drowned boat's name again.

events.title: A wind-name is cut at Seann Chwen
events.body: A cutter of that household sets one of Na h-Ochd Gaothan' names beside Seann-Dhaoine' own marks on the great boulder at Seann Chwen, choosing that stone, by his own word, because the name wanted a stone already old.

events.title: A family takes up the old burial ground unasked
events.body: Kin new to that country begin clearing the thorn from the old burial ground's rows each spring though none of their own dead lie there, and within a few years every household near it has come to trust the keeping to them alone.

events.title: Diggers break into a slab-lined grave
events.body: Cutting a new row further back than any before it, the keepers' own diggers break into an older grave lined close with cut slabs in the manner of Seann-Dhaoine; they close it as carefully as they opened it and move the row a spear's length off.

events.title: No digger tries the older grave again
events.body: The keeping family's eldest holds that a ground kept for the dead does not want its keepers asking after graves it was never given to keep, and no digger of that ground troubles the older grave a second time.

events.title: Pilgrims begin sitting at Coille Naomh Muileann chiar
events.body: People from households that have never before walked so far begin coming singly and in pairs to sit a single night at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, keeping a small fire that burns out before morning, and go home saying only that the night leaves them quieter.

events.title: Settlers from An Cnoc Ruadh raise the first house at Cnoc bheag
events.body: Households come down from An Cnoc Ruadh to build at the edge of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, taking timber only from the river's far side and never from the unclaimed wood, a line later marked by a row of unhewn stones.

events.title: A child of Cnoc bheag is lost past the stones
events.body: A boy not yet seven goes missing near the line of stones at Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag's edge; the settlement and its neighbours search three days into the wood without one sign of him.

events.title: Iain among the searchers who stop at the stones
events.body: Lame still from the passes, Iain of Muileann bhàn joins the search at Cnoc bheag and is the first to say aloud that a wood no household will fell or build nearer than its own river is not a wood that gives back what it takes; the searchers stop at the line of stones, and no teller lays the stopping at their door.

events.title: Iain goes to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh
events.body: Seven-and-twenty years lame, and told by a neighbour of a warm water under the mountain that has eased other travellers' old hurts, Iain walks south on his stick and sits in the pool at first light, the heat working into the crooked hip as no binding ever had.

events.title: Iain walks home whole; the cure-tale is set
events.body: Iain stays three days at the warm water and walks the road home to Muileann bhàn on his own two legs without the stick, in half the days the journey south had cost him; his own household, seeing him come up the rise, takes him at first for a stranger. The tale kept of it is the oldest cure the springs are told for: he came lame, and he walked home.

events.title: Two herders see Marbh-bheò on the ridge
events.body: Caught by dark on the way home, two herders near Marbh-bheò's hills see a shape walk the ridge above them showing no breath in the bitter cold, though their own hangs white before them; they had lit no fire that evening, and so, the telling says, they lived.

events.title: Peigi Dhubh dies on An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: Peigi Dhubh, who laid the stone landing and kept the tallies straighter than her father, dies on An Cnoc Ruadh in her seventy-sixth year, having held it five-and-thirty years; her boats go out the morning after her burying as she asked.

events.title: The covered hearth spreads and the night rule hardens
events.body: The pit-dug, stone-lidded hearth spreads from Marbh-bheò's hills toward the settlements nearer Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, and it hardens there into a rule no council ever set: no open fire is lit on those slopes after dark.

events.title: Caol mhòr's settlers set aside the marked midden stones
events.body: Households raising walls from Seann-Dhaoine' shell midden at Caol mhòr will not turn a stone that carries a mark, cut or worn, and lay those aside in an unmortared line along the shore, so that two kinds of wall stand side by side there ever after.

events.title: Somhairle walks the ground at Baile chrom
events.body: Somhairle finds the resettled fields at Baile chrom already byred and welled, and Donnchadh Ruadh shows him the old field-marks still standing half sunk beneath the new grass, ploughed by hands no household there now names aloud.

events.title: The last thicket on Rathad an t-Salainn is cut through
events.body: Carriers weary of the long way round cut through the last unbroken stand of thorn and birch on Rathad an t-Salainn to the north-west, so that Muileann àrsaidh stands a full day nearer the pans of Baile ghorm than it had ever stood before.

events.title: The first bank is turned east of the old workings
events.body: Settlers pushing toward the rising country dig a ditch and raise the spoil behind it at Dùn thais, a ring of earth built without any word sent from Dùn ìseal and without any word sent back once it stood.

events.title: Fire clears the heavy ground at Achadh chaol
events.body: Across three dry summers the households of Achadh chaol burn back the old scrub a field's width at a time and plough the black ground while the ash still holds its warmth, taking the first year a crop the older fields to the west had not equalled in a generation.

events.title: The last course is set on Cuan ruadh's wall
events.body: The households of Cuan ruadh finish laying stone to the eaves the whole circuit of the settlement, the first roofs on that coast built to stand against wind rather than merely to be raised again once it has passed.

events.title: A well is opened within Cathair fhada's bank
events.body: Cathair fhada digs and lines a well inside its own earthwork, so that a household need not send its water-carriers down to the shore while a storm still has teeth in it.

events.title: Caol ruadh's fishers mark the strait's channels
events.body: The fishers of the narrow strait take to tying woven buoys over the deep channels where the current runs hardest, a small custom that spreads along the coast in a carrier's mouth the way the paired tide-marks spread before it.

events.title: Households come down to Doire ghlas
events.body: Families out of the near valleys settle in the grove where the king kept his seven nights, drawn by its shelter and its old cleared paths, and mark timber in the oaks themselves for the first of their new byres.

events.title: Somhairle asks the household to spare three oaks
events.body: Finding the three oldest trunks of the grove marked for the axe, Somhairle asks Fearchar mac Ailig's household to take their roof-beams elsewhere, giving no reason beyond that his father once set six pots beneath those particular trees.

events.title: The three oaks are spared
events.body: The household cuts its beams instead from younger growth a short walk east and leaves the three old trunks standing at the centre of the new settlement, ringed within a generation by houses that call the place only the ring under the oaks.

events.title: Somhairle finds grey in his beard
events.body: A cheese-seller on the road through the near valleys remarks on the grey coming into Somhairle's beard, and he finds at a still pool that she has told him true: the first lines his face has shown in two thousand four hundred and thirty-five years.

events.title: Beathan sees his father's face has changed
events.body: Coming on Somhairle unexpectedly at the slab, Beathan stops in the doorway before he crosses it, having seen in his father's face the beginning of an ageing neither of them has yet spoken of aloud.

events.title: Murchadh rides north to hold the plain
events.body: The king sends his son Murchadh north with sixty households to hold the northern plain in his name, the first of the king's sons given ground beyond the settled valleys to keep rather than merely to pass through.

events.title: Baile Mòr mhòr rises round the spring that never freezes
events.body: Murchadh raises his hall on a rise above a spring that runs clear through every winter, and the households of the plain name the place Baile Mòr mhòr before it has earned the size of the name; within four centuries it stands eighty houses, the largest place north of An Cnoc Ruadh.

events.title: Sheep-households settle Baile gharbh
events.body: Households take up the stony ground north-east of Murchadh's spring, keep sheep where the land will bear nothing heavier, and send their wool south along the coast road to Cruinneachadh an Àtha rather than north to Murchadh's own granary.

events.title: Baile fhiadhaich settled among the boar-thickets
events.body: Settlers build on the western coast where the boars run heaviest, hang tusks over their doors, and take boar for their chief meat; the island comes to know a man of that place by his gait, from a lifetime of walking ground a boar might break from underfoot.

events.title: Cuan shean settled beside the old landing
events.body: Households take up a harbour beside a stone landing built by hands none of them can name, older than any wall near it, and use it as they find it rather than mend it, out of the caution settlers keep wherever Seann-Dhaoine' work still stands.

events.title: Eithne nic Ailein is born
events.body: A daughter is born to the king in the near valleys and named Eithne; she grows quicker of tongue than most of her father's blood troubles to be, and comes north, in time, to hold ground of her own rather than sit idle at any hearth.

events.title: The first of Murchadh's eleven sons is born
events.body: The eldest of eleven sons is born to Murchadh over the better part of three centuries; each, coming of an age to want it, is given a corner of the plain to hold under his father rather than a place idle at his hearth.

events.title: Dùn chrom is raised with its bank facing two ways
events.body: Herders wanting the bank to face south and quarrymen wanting it to face north raise, between them, a single crooked earthwork that answers both wants at once and satisfies neither fully, and the bent fort stands from its first year with a name that fits it more ways than its builders meant.

events.title: Eilidh Ghlas dies
events.body: Eilidh Ghlas, who sent her younger son west to be raised and knew him at the door when he came home, dies in her seven hundred and thirtieth year; both her sons stand at her burying, and the list keeps only one of them.

events.title: Tobar dhearg rises round the red well
events.body: The keepers of a beacon on the southern cape build at last round a well whose water runs faintly red from the rock, and their settlement grows into the greatest place on that coast, its fire burning nightly for ships that have learned to watch for it.

events.title: The holders of Dùn chrom and Dùn thais quarrel over which way a bank should face
events.body: Ruadhan Beag of Dùn chrom and the holder of Dùn thais fall into two winters of hard words over which way a bank ought to face, until Murchadh rides to hear them and leaves the ditch as it stands, finding a hundred years without an enemy a better argument than either holder makes against it.

events.title: Beathan mac Shomhairle dies at Tobar dhìreach
events.body: Beathan, son of Somhairle, who sat his nights at the slab since before Murchadh was born, dies in his two thousand two hundred and thirteenth year, the oldest death yet counted among the king's kin; the households of the north, hearing the number, begin for the first time to reckon what it may mean to outlive a holder's holder.

events.title: Eithne's households name the ground below Làrach an Dùin-fhaire Cathair mhòr
events.body: Settlers below a broken watch-tower ask Eithne, then a hundred and forty-four years old, to lay out their fields, and she stays; her households name the place Cathair mhòr, the great city, out of hope rather than size, and take no stone from the ruin above them.

events.title: Households come to Cnoc naomh for its spring
events.body: Settlers take up a hill already called, by no teller then living able to say why, the holy hill, and keep its water and the fact of its holiness together without asking more of either.

events.title: Muileann naomh is founded on piles over the marsh
events.body: The first houses of Muileann naomh stand on driven piles over standing marsh water between Tobar dhearg and the old Seann Skell, and are afterward moved to firm ground a bowshot inland once the piles prove the footing sound, keeping the name the marsh first gave them.

events.title: The king takes back the western valleys from Murchadh
events.body: After three hundred years in Murchadh's keeping, the king takes back the poorer western valleys of the northern plain and gives them to a grandson of An Cnoc Ruadh's line, saying only that the ground had grown crowded enough to want a nearer hand; Murchadh does not argue it, and the plain stops speaking of it within the year.

events.title: Calum Ciar dies at Dùn ìseal
events.body: Calum Ciar, eleventh to hold Dùn ìseal under the king, dies in his seven hundred and eleventh year, having asked the slab for its lot once and never asked again; the king buries him on the hill beside his mother.

events.title: Diorbhail born at Tobar dhìreach
events.body: A daughter is born to a household of the watch at Tobar dhìreach and named Diorbhail; she will say her own line back before she can tie a shoe, and carry Sloinneadh a' Chlachair after Somhairle.

events.title: Diorbhail says her own line before she can tie a shoe
events.body: A child of Tobar dhìreach not yet three years old says her line back four generations at her mother's fire, for the pleasure of the saying and not because she is asked, and the households of Na Glinn Àrda begin to remark on her the way a valley remarks on any child who does an ordinary thing early.

events.title: Somhairle first sits Diorbhail by the slab
events.body: Somhairle takes the seven-year-old Diorbhail up to the slab for a morning, on no more of an asking than that her mother has no need of her, and gives her the small tellings that ring the Line rather than the Line itself, holding that a thing given too soon to too young a head is given badly.

events.title: The summons to An Cruinneachadh Mòr reaches the north
events.body: Riders of the king's own household bring word to Baile Mòr mhòr that every holder of every share of the island is to come to a gathering at the ford of salt and wool greater than any before it; Murchadh sends word to his sons and to Eithne, and rides south himself with sixty of his household.

events.title: An Cnoc Ruadh's salt-traders walk to An Cruinneachadh Mòr
events.body: Word goes out along every road that Cruinneachadh an Àtha in the three thousandth year since the grove will be kept greater than any before it. Households of An Cnoc Ruadh's lake shore, among them An Cnoc Ruadh girl and her mother, walk the fourteen miles down with their salt wrapped against the damp.
